body:
# Ouranós, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *ouranos*. This is the file on how **Ouranós** replaced it.

Ouranós is the first tyrant of Greek cosmogony: a father who fears his children and is destroyed by one of them. His fall sets the pattern of divine succession. After Chaos and Gē came Ouranós, 'starry' and equal to her in size.  He covered Gē on every side and became the secure seat of the blessed gods.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ouranós
- **ASCII form:** ouranos
- **Meaning:** "Heaven, sky"
- **Domain of influence:** Sky
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Οὐρανός
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 185 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Οὐρανός**. On the evidence, it means "Heaven, sky".

Strip **Ouranós** to *ouranos* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ó** — Acute on o: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Ouranós** lives at [/sites/ouranos/](/sites/ouranos/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ouranos/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ouranos/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ouranos/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Ouranós** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Space, Astronomy & Celestial Science** — Heaven personified — and the planet Uranus keeps his name.
- **Aviation & Aerospace** — Heaven personified; the destination above the weather.
- **Ancestry & Heritage Services** — Father of Titans, Cyclopes, and Hundred-Handers; every Olympian pedigree opens with his line.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
